messages:
ana: Heads-up: after re-running quant calibration for qwen-7b (4-bit recipe) we see tail latency regressions on small requests — ~35% p99 increase. Not on large batches.
max: saw the spike on the nightly dashboard too. p50 unchanged, p95 up ~10%, p99 up ~35%. Perf traces show more kernel fallbacks around attention matmul.
devon: curious — did calibration change activation ranges or per-channel vs per-tensor scales? even small shifts can flip kernel selection heuristics.
sasha: I compared the old and new quant profiles — layer_norm outputs have slightly higher outliers after the new calibrator. That seems to force the runtime to avoid the INT4 fast path for some layers.
max: attaching quick profile snippet from the run: ```
# perf summary (qwen-7b 4-bit, small burst)
KV store hits: 87%
KV broken-shards: 0
GEMM kernels invoked: fp16_gemm 62%, int4_fast_gemm 18%, fallback_fp16_gemm 20%
Latency p99: 312ms  (baseline 232ms)
```
ana: @devon can you check if KV cache dtype coercion or rounding changed after quantized KV storage was introduced? If cached key/value tensors get cast to fp16 when kernel wants int8/int4 it might cause extra copies.
devon: checked: when the profile uses per-channel scales we now store per-shard scale metadata in the KV header. But older retrieval path does an extra .to(dtype) in some branches. That triggers a memcpy and blocks async copy -> increases tail.
perf-bot: [alert] regression-detected: qwen-7b-4bit tail-latency up >25% vs baseline-2026-03-10. Ticket auto-created: PERF-4821.
sasha: action items I propose: 1) reproduce locally with the new calibrator + minimal batch size 1; 2) force kernel selection override to int4_fast for problematic layers to confirm causality; 3) add unit to ensure KV retrieval never does blocking cast on hot path.
max: I ran a quick override test: forcing int4_fast for decoder attn reduces p99 down to baseline but increases some per-token CPU scheduling overhead. Still better than the fallback.
nana: we should also add model-specific quant profile entries to our config repo (redwood/quant-profiles) with keys: model-family, calibrator-seed, per-layer-exceptions, preferred-kernel. Share snippet: ```json
{"model":"qwen-7b","recipe":"4bit-channelwise","calibrator_seed":"42","exceptions":[{"layer_index":17,"preferred_kernel":"int4_fast_gemm"}],"kv_header":"per-shard-scales-v1"}
```
devon: +1. I'll open a PR with the profile + test harness that runs inference with `--override-kernel` and asserts p99 <= baseline*1.05 for small requests.
sasha: also flag: Llama/mistral variants need separate calibrator configs; mixing datasets for calibration caused inconsistent extremes. For Mistral I recommend using the longer-context corpus, Qwen prefers dialogue-heavy samples.
max: can we add runtime telemetry to record which kernel a layer used for each request (sampled 1%)? would help debugging future regressions.
nana: agreed. Let's land the PR for qwen profile + KV non-blocking fix first. devon, want to pair on the KV change?
devon: yea. I'll pair today. Planning: PR for KV path + unit tests, CI run of quant-profile test matrix, then release-canary.
perf-bot: [ci] runs queued: quant-profiles/pr-99, kv-nonblocking/pr-18. ETA ~40m.
sasha: thanks everyone. I'll update the PERF-4821 ticket with the config snippet and assign to devon/max. :thumbsup:
